findings.source_quote: Καὶ τῶν ἀγαθῶν μοι, φημί, κύριε, δήλωσον τὴν δύναμιν, ἵνα πορευθῶ ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ δουλεύσω αὐτοῖς, ἵνα ἐργασάμενος αὐτὰ δυνηθῶ σωθῆναι.
findings.english_quote: Sir, also explain the power of good things. I want to walk in them and serve them, so that by doing them I may be able to be saved.
findings.issue: The first purpose clause, introduced by ἵνα, states the purpose of requesting the explanation: so that Hermas may walk in and serve the good things. Replacing it with the independent assertion “I want” adds an explicit statement of desire and leaves that explanatory purpose relation unexpressed. The second purpose clause concerning salvation is retained.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “Sir, also explain the power of good things, so that I may walk in them and serve them, and by doing them may be able to be saved.”

summary: Both editions were compared independently with all twelve paragraphs of the supplied working Greek. The standard has no identified concrete fidelity defect. The simplified edition needs a localized correction to the purpose relation in paragraph 8. Both retain the difficult good/evil assertions, necessity, negations, salvation language, servant terminology, and disclosed working readings without harmonizing the stated alternatives. Acceptance concerns fidelity to the supplied working source and disclosure, not verification of unseen plates, editions, handwriting, or exhaustive collation. The proposed correction remains subject to fresh review.
